title: GSC dialect profile
description: One game's GSC dialect as feature flags, modelled on Clang LangOptions and gscode GameProfile. Validates profiles/<engine-id>.toml after TOML parsing. The parser accepts the superset; a profile decides what is reported as not available in this game.

id.description: Engine id, as used by gsc-tool and acts where they have one.

dialect_family.description: Syntax lineage. iw: #include merge, ::f pointers. treyarch-pre-t7: Treyarch games before the BO3 rewrite. treyarch-t7plus: #using and #namespace, &f pointers (includes JUP).

grade.description: verified-on-corpus: the main syntax axes were measured by this project on shipped scripts. documented: values come from cited tools and docs. core: no game-specific evidence; values are carried from a sibling.

bare_call_resolution.description: Builtin call style: how an unqualified call `foo()` (and `&foo` / `::foo`) resolves. builtin-first (measured in no game; despite the name the same file comes before the builtins): a function of the same file, then the builtins, then the functions the imports bring in (#include, or with #namespace the current namespace and the #using'd files); a threaded call and `&foo` resolve as a plain call, `::foo` reaches only a function of the same file. gscode's builtin-first (the builtin before every script function; threaded calls and references mean the script function) is closer to builtin-strict; the games that carry builtin-first from it keep this reading until measured. namespace-first: a function of the current namespace, then the builtins, never a function of another namespace even when its file is #using'd; a threaded call never reaches a builtin. file-first: no namespaces; a function of the same file, then the builtin, then the functions of the #include'd files (an #include'd function named like a builtin does not shadow it); a function reference (`::foo`) and a threaded call never reach a builtin. builtin-strict: no namespaces; the builtin before any script function, even one of the same file (only a path-qualified call `path::foo` reaches that function), then a function of the same file, then the functions of the #include'd files; a threaded call never reaches a builtin (the same file, then the #include'd files); a function reference (`::foo`) takes the plain call's order, builtin first (T6 stores the builtin's native handler, which does not run as script).

measure.description: The measurement that will settle the question.

confidence.description: measured-in-engine: measured by this project by running its own scripts in the game's VM, emulated offline from the executable (semantics/<game>.toml). verified-on-corpus: measured by this project on shipped scripts (method in tools/, counts in evidence/). A zero count is weaker: absence of use, not proof of absence. documented: stated by a cited tool, doc or official source. assumed: carried by inference, or only accepted by a community compiler.
